groups.title: Start here
groups.blurb: Set up the machine, see where it stands, keep it current.

commands.name: init
commands.summary: The setup wizard: asks the questions, shows a review, then installs on a progress screen (press v for the live log) and keeps a log file.

commands.name: refresh
commands.summary: Put a managed config back to what BxRig ships, with a backup first and without installing anything.
commands.note: A file you edited is kept and reported; --force overwrites it after a backup (see config history and config restore). --starter also rewrites the starter hyprland.lua or Noctalia config.toml, which are yours.

commands.name: reinstall
commands.summary: Run the setup wizard again from your saved answers (the same as init --rerun).
commands.note: This is the way to install packages again. refresh only puts config files back.

commands.name: wizard
commands.summary: Wizard pieces for scripts: render the demo screens or a pages file.

commands.name: status
commands.summary: What is installed and configured on this machine, compared with what BxRig would do.

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: Checks every tool BxRig needs (git, curl, unzip, jq, Java 21, mvm, bvm, BoxLang, MatchBox, Rust, Cargo), one status line each. Exit 4 when one is missing. --dev adds advice on your developer setup.
commands.note: --dev checks git name and email, an SSH key, the SSH agent, commit signing, a container engine and EDITOR. They print warn with the command that fixes them and never change the exit code.

commands.name: update
commands.summary: Check for a BxRig update, apply it, pick a channel, turn the daily notification on or off.
usage: update check [--notify] | apply [--yes] | channel [stable|beta] | notifications on|off|status [--json]
commands.note: Exit 10 from `update check` means an update is available.

commands.name: scheduler
commands.summary: One scheduler on the BoxLang JVM: the update check, backups, BoxLang checks and your own tasks, with run history.
usage: scheduler remove NAME | enable NAME | disable NAME | pause GROUP | resume GROUP | run NAME [--json]
examples: bxrig scheduler add photos-to-nas --when="daily 23:00" --group=sync -- rsync -a ~/Pictures nas:/photos
bxrig scheduler add tidy-downloads --when="weekly sun 10:00" -- bxrig files tidy
commands.note: WHEN is every N minutes, every N hours, hourly, daily HH:MM, weekdays HH:MM, weekly DAY HH:MM or cron M H DOM MON DOW. install writes the runner (a BoxLang scheduler class) and bxrig-scheduler.service (`boxlang schedule` on it), adds the update check, the file backup and the BoxLang check as tasks, and turns off bxrig-update-check.timer and bxrig-backup.timer; it is a plan until --yes. Every run is recorded in ~/.local/state/bxrig/scheduler/history; a failure sends a notice. Exit 10 from a task counts as "needs attention" where the task lists it as ok.

commands.name: ascii
commands.summary: Text in large letters (FIGlet fonts) or a picture as text art, painted with a colour or a gradient.
commands.note: COLOR is #rrggbb, #rgb, theme (the accent of the theme that is on) or a name (black, white, gray, red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, magenta, pink, boxlang, bxrig). SPEC is a preset (brand, theme, sunset, ocean, fire, forest, candy, rainbow) or two or more colours separated by commas. Without --color or --gradient the brand gradient is used in a terminal and no colour into a pipe; --plain and NO_COLOR leave colour out. With no TEXT the first line of stdin is drawn. `ascii image` draws a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG (read by the embedded bx-image module) WIDTH columns wide (default 48): blocks are half blocks in 24-bit colour, ascii is a brightness ramp in the picture's colours; transparent pixels stay blank.

commands.name: about
commands.summary: About this rig: the BxRig laptop logo beside the hardware, your dev stack and the look (fastfetch).
commands.note: Runs fastfetch with ~/.config/bxrig/fastfetch.jsonc; the logo (~/.config/bxrig/theme/fastfetch-logo.ans) follows the theme and is rewritten by `bxrig theme set`. A missing logo or config is written first. Without fastfetch the logo, version and tagline are shown. --wait asks for Enter before returning (the launcher's About window uses it).

commands.name: banner
commands.summary: The BXRIG wordmark in block letters, painted in the colors of the current theme (the retro greeting).
commands.note: Five rows, painted top to bottom with the theme's accent, magenta and cyan. A pipe, --plain and NO_COLOR give plain text; --json gives the lines and the three colors.

commands.name: version
commands.summary: The BxRig version and build.

commands.name: menu
commands.summary: The control center: every command as a menu on your launcher (Rofi, Walker, Wofi, Fuzzel or Vicinae).
usage: menu | menu items [--json] | menu search TEXT [--json] | menu open [ROUTE] [--json]
commands.note: Bind it to a key; the first entry, Search, lists every entry as one flat list. `menu open ROUTE` opens one submenu (system, capture, toggle, hardware, agent, shortcuts, trigger > capture); `menu open` lists the routes. A tick marks the current value (bar position, dock, window look, theme mode, power profile). Entries that do not apply here are hidden (laptop, touchpad, touchscreen, webcam, hybrid GPU, Hyprland, Plasma, installed apps); Install hides apps you have. Your own ~/.config/bxrig/menu.json adds entries (a program or a bxrig command under a submenu id), hides and renames entries by id: `menu ids` lists the ids, `menu file --yes` writes an example, `menu file` checks yours.

commands.name: apps
commands.summary: Your installed catalog apps, as a list or a launcher grid.

commands.name: help
commands.summary: This list, or the usage of one command. `bxrig --help` and `bxrig -h` print the same list.

groups.title: Install and remove
groups.blurb: Apps from the catalog, any package from the repositories or the AUR, and the reverse.

commands.name: install
commands.summary: Install catalog apps by id (or a whole group or profile).
commands.note: With no name it installs the default set; without --yes it prints the plan and changes nothing.

commands.name: remove
commands.summary: Uninstall catalog apps (their packages or web launchers).
commands.note: Protected packages (the base system, the kernel, bxrig itself) are refused.

commands.name: pkg
commands.summary: Search, inspect, install and remove any package from the repositories and the AUR.
usage: pkg search TEXT [--source=all|repo|aur] [--limit=N] | info NAME | installed [--explicit] | install NAME... [--aur] [--yes] [--dry-run] | remove NAME... [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: catalog
commands.summary: Browse the app catalog.
usage: catalog list [--group=G] [--category=C] [--tier=default|optional] [--kind=K] [--source=S] [--distro=D] [--json] | show ID [--distro=D] | groups | check | coverage [--distro=D] | version

commands.name: plan
commands.summary: Show what installing would do, without doing it.

commands.name: install-plan
commands.summary: The install plan for the selection (same as plan).

commands.name: optional-plan
commands.summary: The plan for the optional apps.

commands.name: profile-plan
commands.summary: The plan for one profile.

commands.name: profile-install-plan
commands.summary: The install steps for one profile.

commands.name: profile-install
commands.summary: Install a profile (jvm, containers, terminal, editors, ...).

commands.name: optional-install
commands.summary: Install the optional apps of the catalog.

commands.name: profile-list
commands.summary: List the profiles.

commands.name: optional-list
commands.summary: List the optional apps.

commands.name: desktop-list
commands.summary: List the desktop apps in the catalog.

commands.name: tui-list
commands.summary: List the terminal apps in the catalog.

commands.name: web-list
commands.summary: List the web apps in the catalog.

commands.name: package-status
commands.summary: Whether a catalog app is installed.

commands.name: package-source
commands.summary: Where a catalog app comes from (pacman, AUR, PKGBUILD, web).

commands.name: dev-plan
commands.summary: What the developer toolchain install would use: Java 21, Maven, Gradle, BVM, MVM.

commands.name: prerequisites
commands.summary: The same check as doctor: one status line per tool BxRig needs.

commands.name: apps-doctor
commands.summary: Checks the catalog apps for missing or broken installs.

commands.name: web
commands.summary: Web apps: create one from a URL, install a set (Google, Microsoft, Apple, BoxLang).
usage: web add [NAME URL] [--browser=brave|chromium|google-chrome|edge|firefox] [--yes] | list | rm NAME [--yes] | install google|microsoft|apple|boxlang|all [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: toolchain
commands.summary: Language toolchains outside the always-installed BoxLang one (Node via nvm, Rust, Python, Go, PHP).
usage: toolchain node [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]   (Bun and Deno: bxrig install bun deno)

groups.title: Desktop setup
groups.blurb: Hyprland with Noctalia, or KDE Plasma beside it: the session, the keys, the defaults.

commands.name: setup
commands.summary: Set up a desktop: Hyprland with Noctalia, Plasma with HyprKwin tiling, terminals, keyboards, status.
usage: setup plasma [--keys | --undo-keys] | hyprland [--terminal=ghostty|kitty|alacritty|foot|konsole] [--layout=dwindle|master|columns|scrolling|monocle|floating] [--workspaces=N] [--natural-scroll] [--layouts=us-intl,es] [--theme=dark|light|auto] [--wallpaper=box|grid|aurora|minimal] | terminal [--default=ghostty] [--also=a,b] | shell [--shell=zsh|fish|bash] | keyboard [--layouts=us-intl,es] | xremap [--build=hypr|kde] | undo plasma|hyprland|xremap | status [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: session
commands.summary: Which desktop SDDM starts: Hyprland or Plasma.

commands.name: tiling
commands.summary: Tiling inside Plasma (HyprKwin): on, off, status, layouts.

commands.name: plasma
commands.summary: Plasma extras: panel layouts (apply, undo, status) and the islands preset.

commands.name: keys
commands.summary: The shortcut table: show, search, run, rebind, check conflicts, apply to Hyprland and Plasma, Traditional or Mac style.
usage: keys show | search TEXT | run ID | style [traditional|mac] [--keyboard=pc|apple] [--swap=on|off] [--yes] | mac [on|off|status] [--yes] | set ID KEYS [--yes] [--force] | reset ID [--yes] | conflicts | sheet | render xremap|hyprland|plasma | check | apply [--yes] [--dry-run] [--force] [--json]
commands.note: Two styles share one table: Traditional (classic Super-key tiling keys) and Mac (Cmd-style keys through xremap). The Mac style on a PC keyboard swaps Alt and Win; an Apple keyboard never swaps. `keys conflicts` checks the table, the remaps of the style that is on and your own hl.bind lines.

commands.name: runner
commands.summary: Which launcher and which menu program BxRig uses (Rofi, Walker, Wofi, Fuzzel, Vicinae).
usage: runner list | show | doctor | launch | select JSON_ENTRIES [--prompt=TEXT] | set PROVIDER | menu-set PROVIDER | icon-theme NAME|auto | launcher-command PROVIDER JSON_ARGV | menu-command PROVIDER JSON_ARGV [--json]

commands.name: launcher
commands.summary: Vicinae as BxRig's launcher: the BxRig theme, BxRig's actions as script commands, and file search.
commands.note: setup is a plan until --yes: it makes Vicinae the launcher and the menu, writes ~/.local/share/vicinae/themes/bxrig.toml (rewritten by every `bxrig theme set`) and selects it with `vicinae theme set bxrig`, writes the script commands to ~/.local/share/vicinae/scripts/bxrig and starts `vicinae server` when it is not running. Vicinae's settings.json is never edited. files opens vicinae://launch/files/search with QUERY typed in.

commands.name: default
commands.summary: Default apps: browser, terminal, file manager.
usage: default show | browser ID | terminal ID | filemanager ID | editor neovim|vscode|zed|kate [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
commands.note: editor sets the app for text files (xdg-mime) and EDITOR and VISUAL in ~/.config/environment.d/50-bxrig-editor.conf (from the next login).

commands.name: layout
commands.summary: Window layout at runtime: tile or float (toggle).

commands.name: assets
commands.summary: Brand assets (logo, icon, wallpapers): list, or install them.

commands.name: launchers
commands.summary: A BxRig submenu in your application menu (opt-in): the setup wizard, the runner menu, the Control Center and its pages.
commands.note: `on` writes one entry per page to ~/.local/share/applications (BxRig Databases, ...), each opening `bxrig tui PAGE` in your terminal, and the BxRig icon (16 to 256 px PNGs and the scalable SVG) to ~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/SIZExSIZE/apps/bxrig.png. An entry you edited is kept, never overwritten or removed. `off` (or `bxrig remove launchers`) takes them out again. Nothing is added unless you ask.

commands.name: config
commands.summary: The managed config files: list, diff, apply, restore a backup, history. A file you edited is never overwritten.
usage: config list|diff NAME|apply NAME|restore NAME ID|history [NAME] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--force] [--json]
commands.note: BxRig never overwrites a file you edited; `config status` shows which ones are yours.

groups.title: Look and feel
groups.blurb: Themes, fonts, bar, dock, windows, monitors and power.

commands.name: theme
commands.summary: Themes: 15 bundled (10 community themes, 5 BxRig), set one, light or dark, install from git.
usage: theme list | show NAME | set NAME [--mode=theme|dark|light|auto] [--keep-wallpaper] | random | next | mode theme|dark|light|auto | install GIT_URL [--name=N] [--force] | import PATH [--name=N] [--force] | remove NAME | vscode [--yes] [--dry-run] | status [--dry-run] [--json]
commands.note: A theme colours the bar, terminals, btop, Neovim, GTK and Qt apps, tmux, fzf, launchers and (on Plasma) the colour scheme. VS Code is opt-in.

commands.name: appearance
commands.summary: Bar layout, dock, app grid, battery percentage, windows, animations, layout, fonts and backgrounds, one setting at a time.
commands.note: Settings act at once (no --yes); --dry-run shows the commands. What you choose is remembered, and `appearance apply` pushes it again. `bar layout`, `dock on|off|toggle`, `appgrid` and `battery-percent` rewrite ~/.config/noctalia/config.toml (backup kept; a file with changes of your own needs --yes). The `terminal` app grid style is only stored for now: nothing draws it yet. `icons` is the exception to "act at once": it installs papirus-icon-theme and writes the BxRig icon theme and settings files, so it prints a plan (exit 2) until --yes; `bxrig` (the default after setup) is the BxRig icons over Papirus-Dark, `papirus` is Papirus-Dark alone. `font` is the coding font (terminals, and the shell until an interface font is set); `ui-font` is the font of the bar, panels and GTK apps; `font-rendering` writes ~/.config/fontconfig/conf.d/60-bxrig-rendering.conf (`default` removes it unless you edited it).

commands.name: screensaver
commands.summary: The screensaver: terminal art in the theme's colours on every monitor after a while idle, then the lock.
commands.note: Effects: sweep, laptop, rain, clock, stars, logo; they take turns, a minute each. Defaults: the screensaver after 150 s idle, the lock after 300 s (0 for never), both counted from the start of idle. On Hyprland, Noctalia runs them as idle behaviors (bxrig screensaver start, with stop as the resume command). On Plasma, a user service runs swayidle with the same two commands (start --idle does nothing while Plasma's power manager says something holds the screen awake), a KWin script puts one full-screen window on each screen, and lock= sets Plasma's own lock timeout (whole minutes, rounded up). start opens a full-screen terminal per monitor; preview runs it in this terminal. Any key, click, scroll or mouse move closes it. Settings: ~/.config/bxrig/screensaver.json.

commands.name: hotcorners
commands.summary: Hot corners: an action for each screen corner (overview, notifications, show desktop, lock, launcher, agents, themes).
commands.note: CORNER is top-left, top-right, bottom-left or bottom-right. Hyprland uses Noctalia's hot corners; Plasma uses KWin screen edges (notifications, agents and themes have no Plasma edge action).

commands.name: display
commands.summary: Monitors: scale, rotation, mode, position, mirroring the laptop panel, turning it off, brightness.
commands.note: On Hyprland it writes theme/monitors.lua and reloads; on Plasma it uses kscreen-doctor.

commands.name: power
commands.summary: Laptop power: battery details, profile, lid action on battery and on AC, hibernate, charge limit, setup of the power tools, doctor.
commands.note: `power status --json` has one entry per battery (percent, state, watts, time_remaining_minutes, health_percent, cycles, charge_limit; -1 when unknown) and the lid action on battery and on AC. `power lid ACTION` without battery or ac sets both. `power hibernate` exits 4 unless disk swap (zram does not count), the kernel resume= parameter and the kernel are ready; it is a plan (exit 2) without --yes. `power charge-limit` writes the kernel attribute charge_control_end_threshold and keeps it with a small systemd unit; it exits 4 on a battery without that attribute (not verified on real hardware). `power setup` does nothing on a machine without a battery unless you add --force.

commands.name: time
commands.summary: The time zone: show, set, set from your IP after travelling, follow your location, network time, the bar clock format, and the world clock.
usage: time world [status | set ZONE,ZONE... | add ZONE | remove ZONE | on | off] [--yes] [--json]
commands.note: `time auto on` sends your Wi-Fi networks or IP address to a location web service; the plan says so first. `time format` sets the bar clock's text in Noctalia date format tokens (or MMM d - HH:mm patterns); it acts at once and rewrites the Noctalia config.

commands.name: calendar
commands.summary: Your calendars on this machine (iCal addresses and Google Calendar), kept in sync by vdirsyncer, and the agenda read from them.
examples: bxrig calendar add ical holidays webcal://example.org/holidays.ics
commands.note: BxRig writes its own vdirsyncer config (~/.config/bxrig/vdirsyncer/config, mode 600, passed as VDIRSYNCER_CONFIG), so a vdirsyncer setup of your own is never touched. An iCal address is read only; webcal:// is fetched as https://. Google needs the CalDAV API on and an OAuth client of type Desktop app; the first sync, in a terminal, opens Google's sign-in. With the scheduler installed, adding a calendar adds the task calendar-sync (every 15 minutes). remove deletes only the local copy.

commands.name: remind
commands.summary: A reminder that pops up at a time you choose.
commands.note: Reminders are kept in ~/.config/bxrig/reminders.json. An HH:MM that has passed today means tomorrow. `due` shows the reminders whose time has come as notices; the scheduler task reminders runs it every minute (added with the first reminder when the scheduler is installed).

commands.name: accessibility
commands.summary: Zoom like a Mac, reduce motion, and three high-contrast themes. All off until you turn them on.
commands.note: zoom on makes the zoom keys work: Option+Cmd+8 toggles, Option+Cmd+= zooms in, Option+Cmd+- zooms out (Option is Alt, Cmd is Super). While zoom is off the keys only say how to turn it on. Hyprland zooms around the pointer (cursor:zoom_factor); Plasma uses KWin's Zoom effect. reduce-motion turns off window, bar and app animations. contrast picks bxrig-contrast-dark, bxrig-contrast-light or bxrig-colorblind (every text colour at least 7:1, WCAG AAA); off goes back to your theme. Settings act at once; --dry-run shows the commands.

commands.name: toggle
commands.summary: Quick switches. Today: stay awake (Noctalia caffeine).

commands.name: nightshift
commands.summary: Night light: on, off, toggle, status (sunset to sunrise from your time zone).

commands.name: notify
commands.summary: Notifications through Noctalia: do not disturb, snooze, clear, and notices for the time, battery and weather.
usage: notify dnd on|off|toggle|status | snooze [30m|2h|90s|off] | clear [--history] | time | battery | weather [--json]
commands.note: time, battery and weather show one notice through notify-send. weather asks wttr.in over the network.

groups.title: System and security
groups.blurb: Updates, snapshots, DNS, kernels, keys and secrets.

commands.name: system
commands.summary: See what is waiting to be updated, update the system (a snapshot first), lock, suspend, log out, reboot, shut down.
commands.note: updates only reads: repository and AUR counts and the package list, and whether a restart is needed (exit 4 without checkupdates from pacman-contrib). update takes a snapshot first, then updates the repository (--repo), the AUR (--aur, exit 4 without yay or paru) or both (--all, the default). lock and suspend act at once; logout, reboot and shutdown need --yes (the menu asks first). restart shell stops and starts Noctalia (or restarts Plasma's plasmashell service); audio restarts PipeWire and WirePlumber; wifi and bluetooth unblock the radio and turn it on. password runs passwd on your terminal. firmware asks fwupd (LVFS: BIOS/UEFI, SSDs, docks) for updates; update installs them on your terminal. speedtest network runs speedtest-cli; disk writes and reads 1 GiB in ~/.cache with direct I/O; dns is dns bench; last shows the last result of each test (only the latest is kept, in ~/.local/state/bxrig/speedtest-last.json).

commands.name: security
commands.summary: Fingerprint and security key for sudo, SSH server, passwordless sudo, with guards.
commands.note: Only /etc/pam.d/sudo is ever changed, with a `sufficient` line and a backup; sudoers is checked with visudo first. `--dry-run` prints the exact line.

commands.name: dns
commands.summary: DNS servers of the active connections: Cloudflare, Google, Quad9, your own, or back to DHCP. bench times each one to pick the fastest.

commands.name: kernel
commands.summary: List, install and remove kernels. Never edits the bootloader.
usage: kernel list | install NAME | remove NAME [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: ssh
commands.summary: Create an SSH key (ed25519; an existing one is kept).

commands.name: git
commands.summary: Sign commits and tags with your SSH key.
commands.note: on sets gpg.format ssh, user.signingkey, commit.gpgsign and tag.gpgsign, and adds your email and key to ~/.config/git/allowed_signers so git can verify. It needs the key (bxrig ssh key --yes) and git user.email. off stops signing and keeps the key. Add the key to GitHub as a Signing key for the Verified badge.

commands.name: secrets
commands.summary: API keys and tokens in the system keyring, loaded per command, exported encrypted.
usage: secrets status | setup [--keyring=kwallet|gnome-keyring|none] [--yes] | list [--type=ai|other] | set NAME [--from-file=F] [--type=ai|other] [--provider=ID] | get NAME [--show] | unset NAME --yes | apply [--yes] | global on NAME --yes|off NAME|show | unlock | lock | export FILE [--plain] [--force] --yes | import FILE [--overwrite] --yes | env [NAMES...] | run [NAMES...] [--strict] -- COMMAND [ARGS...] [--json]

commands.name: vpn
commands.summary: VPNs in one list: saved NetworkManager profiles and the VPN apps (NordVPN, NordLayer, Tailscale, Mullvad); connect, disconnect, pick a place.
commands.note: NAME is a provider from `vpn list` (nordvpn, nordlayer, tailscale, mullvad) or a saved profile as listed there (`nm:Home`). Choosing one disconnects the one that is connected first, unless `allow_several=true` (Tailscale next to another VPN; routes and DNS can clash). connect and disconnect act at once and take `--dry-run`; `set` and `nordvpn setup` need `--yes`. The providers are data (`catalog/vpn-providers.json`, extend with `~/.config/bxrig/vpn-providers.json`). `list` is empty when no VPN is installed; the other verbs exit 4 then. `--location` takes a value from `vpn locations NAME` (`default` connects as it is, `none` clears a Tailscale exit node). The top bar VPN icon (plugin `bxrig/vpn`) is the same list.

commands.name: cloud
commands.summary: Cloud storage with rclone: remotes, mounts as systemd user units.
usage: cloud remotes | configure | mount NAME [--path=DIR] [--yes] | unmount NAME [--yes] | status [--json]

commands.name: settings
commands.summary: Export and import your BxRig settings as one archive.

commands.name: dotfiles
commands.summary: Apply your dotfiles repo with chezmoi, yadm, stow or plain links, never overwriting unasked, with undo.
usage: dotfiles plan REPO [--method=chezmoi|yadm|stow|links] | apply REPO [--method=M] [--overwrite] [--yes] [--dry-run] | status | undo [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: nas
commands.summary: Your NAS boxes: find them, save their details, list shares, mount them (also automatically), test them, mirror folders to them, use one as a backup target.
usage: nas list | show NAME | remove NAME [--yes]
examples: bxrig nas auto on synology backups --yes
commands.note: SMB mounts are made by root, so the password is also kept in /etc/bxrig/nas/NAME.cred (mode 600); the plan says so. The SMB version is negotiated unless you give --vers. Nothing on the NAS is deleted unless you add --delete to a sync.

commands.name: backup
commands.summary: Backups of your BxRig setup, of the system and of your files, and a way to move them around.
examples: bxrig backup data target add do --type=s3 --endpoint=https://nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com --bucket=mybackups --ask-keys
commands.note: A config snapshot is taken by itself before update, system update, init, reinstall and refresh (turn it off with backup config auto off). Secrets and SSH keys are never in it unless you add --with-secrets, which stores your secrets export, encrypted with a passphrase you type.

commands.name: timemachine
commands.summary: BxTimeMachine: every backup of your system, setup and files on one timeline, with browse, restore, export and send.
commands.note: It needs a terminal (also available as bxtimemachine). Restore, export, send and back up now show the plan first and change nothing until you press y. --local skips the network targets so it opens at once; --demo shows made-up data and runs nothing.

commands.name: java
commands.summary: Your Java homes: list them, install a JDK (through SDKMAN when you have it), choose the default for new shells.
usage: java list | available | install MAJOR|IDENTIFIER [--yes] [--dry-run] | default ID|MAJOR [--yes] | default --unset [--yes] | remove ID [--yes] | env [ID|MAJOR] [--json]
commands.note: Homes come from SDKMAN, BxRig's own Temurin installs (~/.local/share/bxrig/java) and /usr/lib/jvm. With SDKMAN installed (bxrig sdk setup) installs and removals go through it: a major like 21 picks the newest Temurin, an identifier like 21.0.13.0+9-tem installs exactly that. Without it a Temurin JDK is downloaded straight from Adoptium. The system's own JDKs are never deleted. The default is written to java.sh and java.fish, which the shell starters source, so run bxrig refresh shell once on an existing setup.

commands.name: sdk
commands.summary: Java, Maven and Gradle through SDKMAN: install, switch, remove.
usage: sdk status | setup [--yes] | list java|maven|gradle | available java|maven|gradle | install CANDIDATE VERSION [--yes] | default CANDIDATE VERSION [--yes] | remove CANDIDATE VERSION [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
commands.note: setup installs SDKMAN into ~/.sdkman without touching your shell files. Maven and Gradle reach your shells through ~/.config/bxrig/sdk.sh and sdk.fish, which the shell starters source (bxrig refresh shell on an existing setup). Version lists come from api.sdkman.io.

commands.name: mail
commands.summary: A mail catcher for development: a local inbox for the mail your apps send, in a container.
usage: mail start [--keep] [--smtp-port=N] [--ui-port=N] [--yes] | stop | status | remove [--keep-data] [--yes] | list [--limit=N] | show ID | delete ID [--yes] | clear [--yes] | open [ID] | test [--to=ADDR] [--subject=TEXT] | env [--dry-run] [--json]
commands.note: Runs Mailpit in a container (the engine bxrig db engine chose). SMTP is 127.0.0.1:1025 and the web inbox is http://127.0.0.1:8025, both local only. Mail is thrown away when the catcher stops unless you start it with --keep. The Control Center has a Mail page that refreshes by itself.

commands.name: tui
commands.summary: Control Center: every BxRig screen in one terminal, or one page on its own.
commands.note: It needs a terminal. `bxrig tui` opens the Control Center with the sidebar; `bxrig tui PAGE` opens that page alone with the sidebar collapsed, like an app of its own (an unknown page exits 2). The backslash key or Ctrl+b (or a click on the left strip or the breadcrumb) opens and closes the sidebar, Tab and Shift+Tab still change page, and Left opens a collapsed sidebar. --sidebar and --no-sidebar force it either way; below 90 columns it starts collapsed. Nothing is remembered. `tui list` prints the page ids and titles. Enter on a warning shows the plan of the fix before anything changes. --json prints a page's data without a terminal; --demo shows made-up data and runs nothing. Icons are Nerd Font glyphs: on when a Nerd Font is installed, or force them with --icons=on|off or BXRIG_ICONS. `tui apps` is the Apps manager: Installed, Discover and Updates tabs, a search box that is always there, install and remove with a plan first (see the Apps guide).

commands.name: bxtimemachine
commands.summary: The same as timemachine: BxTimeMachine, your backups through time.

commands.name: privacy
commands.summary: What leaves this machine: which AI runs where, your keys, agent data, MCP servers, telemetry; and switches for local only and telemetry.

groups.title: Develop
groups.blurb: BoxLang, editors, databases, containers, virtual machines and AI agents.

commands.name: boxlang
commands.summary: BoxLang status, MatchBox home, logs and .env, modules (ForgeBox), the VS Code extension, links.
usage: boxlang status | check | update [--yes] [--dry-run] | home [--open] | run FILE [ARGS...] | repl | use VERSION [--json]
boxlang modules list|search TEXT|installed|outdated [--json] | install SLUG... | update [SLUG...] | remove SLUG... [--yes] [--dry-run]

boxlang servers [list] | status NAME | add PATH [--name=NAME] | scan DIR [--depth=N] [--yes] | remove NAME | start|stop|restart NAME [--dry-run] | log NAME [--follow] | open NAME | folder NAME [--json]
boxlang matchbox use VERSION | matchbox status | matchbox log-level LEVEL [--yes] | matchbox env list|set KEY VALUE|unset KEY [--yes] | vscode | links | welcome [--json]
examples: bxrig boxlang matchbox env set OPENAI_API_KEY sk-... --yes
commands.note: check compares the BoxLang you run (the jar next to `boxlang`) with downloads.ortussolutions.com version-latest.properties and runs `bx-module outdated`; it exits 10 when anything is behind, like `update check`. update uses bvm (`bvm install latest`, `bvm use latest`) when it is there, else the quick installer (`install-boxlang latest --non-interactive`). home is BOXLANG_HOME or ~/.boxlang. run and repl hand the terminal to the real `boxlang`. Module commands wrap bx-module; installed and outdated --json give rows. servers registers BoxLang MiniServer apps (miniserver.json) and CommandBox apps (server.json) in ~/.config/bxrig/servers.json; a MiniServer runs detached with its log in ~/.local/state/bxrig/servers, a CommandBox app through `box server start|stop|log directory=PATH`; running means its port is listening.

commands.name: editor
commands.summary: Neovim with LazyVim, the BoxLang plugin and themes that follow the BxRig theme.

usage: vm list | status [NAME] | size [NAME] | info NAME [--show-password] | doctor | versions linux|windows | create windows [NAME] [--version=V] [--ram=8G] [--cpus=N] [--disk=64G] [--share=PATH|none] | create linux NAME [--tag=ubuntu-xfce] [--cpus=N] [--memory=4G] [--share=PATH|none] [--gpu=none|auto|intel|amd|nvidia] | start|stop|logs NAME | open NAME [--web] [--fullscreen] | remove NAME [--keep-data] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]

usage: android [--json] | setup [--vanilla] [--yes] | start | stop | apps | open [APP] | install FILE.apk [--yes] | register [--open] | remove [--data] [--yes] [--json]

usage: skills list [--tag=T] | search TEXT | show OWNER/REPO/SLUG | install [bxrig|boxlang|matchbox|OWNER/REPO/SLUG]... [--yes] | installed | update [--yes] | remove NAME [--yes] | status | link [--json]

groups.title: Everyday tools
groups.blurb: Screenshots, clipboard, windows, dictation and hardware helpers.

commands.name: screenshot
commands.summary: Screenshots: screen, region, window, OCR text, QR codes, a color picker, or a menu.
usage: screenshot screen|region|window [--edit] | ocr | qr | color | menu [--dry-run] [--json]

commands.name: qr
commands.summary: Make a QR code from text (printed in the terminal, or saved with --out).

commands.name: share
commands.summary: Send files, a folder or the clipboard to a phone or computer nearby with LocalSend, or open it to receive.
commands.note: Sending uses LocalSend's command line, localsend-cli (LocalSend 1.18 and later): without --to it lists the devices it finds and you pick one, on your terminal (the menu opens one). Without a path a file chooser asks (kdialog on Plasma, else zenity). clipboard sends what you copied as a text file. receive opens the LocalSend app. Exit 4 when localsend-cli or LocalSend is missing.

commands.name: record
commands.summary: Screen recording: start, stop, toggle, with desktop or microphone audio if you like.
commands.note: --audio=desktop adds what the speakers play, --audio=mic the default microphone (both through pactl). Desktop and microphone together are not offered: wf-recorder takes one audio source. Exit 2 for another audio value. --webcam puts your webcam in a corner while it records (bottom-right unless you name another), so it is in the video; it ends with the recording. Hyprland pins it (the BxRig module's rules); on Plasma it is a small window you can drag.

commands.name: browser
commands.summary: Your default browser in a private window.
commands.note: Reads the default web browser (set by `default browser` or the wizard) and starts it with its private flag: Firefox --private-window, Chromium, Brave and Chrome --incognito, Edge --inprivate. Another browser exits 4.

commands.name: files
commands.summary: Your default file manager in the folder of the focused window.
commands.note: Without DIR it uses the working directory of the focused window's newest child process (Hyprland), else your home folder, and opens it with xdg-open, so `default filemanager` decides which file manager.

commands.name: webcam
commands.summary: A small live webcam preview, on or off with one key.
commands.note: mpv on /dev/video0 in a window of class bxrig-webcam, which the Hyprland module floats and sizes. Exit 4 without mpv or a webcam.

commands.name: clipboard
commands.summary: Clipboard history (cliphist): pick, list, clear, setup.

commands.name: emoji
commands.summary: The emoji picker (rofimoji).

commands.name: forcequit
commands.summary: Pick a window or process and force quit it.

commands.name: window
commands.summary: Minimize, restore and snap windows, and the quake console.
commands.note: quake shows or hides the special workspace qconsole (the default terminal starts there the first time); quake send moves the focused window onto it. snap left|right|top|bottom floats the focused window onto that half of its monitor. Hyprland only. close-all asks every window to close (apps with unsaved work still ask), then goes to workspace 1; tiled-fullscreen makes the app full screen inside its tile (again to undo).

commands.name: overview
commands.summary: The workspace and window overview.

commands.name: quicklook
commands.summary: Quick Look for files (Kiview): preview with a key.

commands.name: dolphin
commands.summary: Dolphin diagnostics: why it is slow or missing features.

commands.name: dictation
commands.summary: Dictation with Superwhisper or Voxtype: setup and toggle.

commands.name: strata
commands.summary: Strata, the file manager: its integrations.

commands.name: gpu
commands.summary: GPU check: driver, rendering, NVIDIA specifics; the mode of a laptop with two GPUs.
commands.note: mode needs two GPUs (counted in /sys/bus/pci/devices) and supergfxctl (supergfxd); a switch is `supergfxctl -m Hybrid|Integrated`, then log out or reboot.

commands.name: input
commands.summary: Input devices: Apple Magic Mouse and Trackpad, Logitech, the helpers for them, the older doctor and trackpad gestures.
commands.note: touchpad and touchscreen switch the device off and on in a Hyprland session (hyprctl eval hl.device); a login turns it back on.

commands.name: audio
commands.summary: Sound server status: outputs, inputs, volumes and the defaults.
commands.note: Read only, through `pactl`. Volume and mixing are in the bar panel (Super+Ctrl+A) and in the terminal mixer in the Hardware menu. Exit 4 when `pactl` is missing or no sound server answers.

commands.name: bluetooth
commands.summary: Bluetooth status: the service, the adapter and the paired devices.
commands.note: Read only, through `bluetoothctl` and `systemctl`. Pairing is in the bar panel (Super+Ctrl+B) and in the terminal UI in the Hardware menu. Exit 4 when `bluetoothctl` is missing.

commands.name: wifi
commands.summary: Wi-Fi status: the radio, the Wi-Fi devices and the network you are on; a QR code to join it.
commands.note: Read only, through `nmcli` (NetworkManager). Joining a network is in the bar panel (Super+Ctrl+N). Exit 4 when `nmcli` is missing. qr draws the network you are on as a QR code a phone camera reads to join (qrencode); the password is in the code only, never printed.

commands.name: airplay
commands.summary: AirPlay receiver: on, off, status.
